messages:
sam: Heads-up: NimbusPay (dedicated pool) reporting a sudden TPS surge and ~30% of requests getting 429s from the admission controller. Started ~08:05 UTC. Token-per-second headroom seems depleted.
anya: Can you paste the root error? 429 body?
sam: Here — from their client logs: `{"error":"admission_rejected","reason":"burst_credits_exhausted","pool":"dedicated-nimbus-01"}`
jorge: Any correlation with autoscale events or recent config changes on that pool?
lena: Checking infra — no recent config rollouts in the last 24h. Autoscaler did not start new nodes; max_replicas was hit at 07:58.
anya: Do we see noisy neighbor on GPU utilization / KV cache eviction?
zephyr-bot: [alert] admission_controller: pool=dedicated-nimbus-01 burst_credits=0 rate_limit=75 tps=220 headroom= -
 (alert id: adc-2401)
jorge: That alert shows burst credits at 0 and steady 220 TPS. Their SLO is 200 TPS with 100 burst credits.
nimbus-support: Customer says they had a marketing push -> short 8-min spike. They expected admission to allow graceful fallthrough but saw 429s across their API keys.
anya: Do we have any auth/billing mismatches? If the credit accounting lagged, some tokens could have been incorrectly charged.
sam: I pulled billing events for their account: last credit update processed 07:52 UTC, then a backlog from 07:58-08:06. There's a 14s processing delay on the credit ledger queue during the spike.
lena: That processing delay + hitting max_replicas explains autoscaler not scaling quickly enough. Also check admission_controller window size — might be smaller than expected causing faster exhaustion.
jorge: Repro steps I'd try: (1) replay a short burst simulating their client at 220 TPS for 8 mins against a staging replica of the pool; (2) instrument admission_controller logs with `adc.debug=true` and dump credit ledger updates; (3) temporarily bump burst_credits for the pool to see if service recovers.
anya: Agreed. Also verify whether any other tenant used cross-pool resources. Could be noisy neighbor consuming GPU slots or KV cache. Queue GPU memory/compute usage for other tenants on same rack.
sam: Quick mitigation: increased pool burst_credits from 100 -> 300 (applied at 08:22 UTC) and triggered scale-up to +2 replicas. Customer confirmed 429s dropped after ~45s.
nimbus-support: Confirmed — client metrics show success rate back to normal. They still want root cause though.
lena: For root cause, capture: admission_controller trace, ledger event timestamps, autoscaler decision logs, and proxy ingress spikes. I'll collect and attach.
jorge: Hypothesis: backlog in ledger processing + autoscaler cooldown prevented timely scaling, while admission window and low initial burst credits made admission reject rather than queueing. Noisy tenant possibility low but not ruled out.
nimbus-support: Also found a stale API client that retried aggressively without backoff — increased effective TPS by ~20% for the burst window. We've asked them to patch.
anya: Action items — owners:
- lena: collect ADC traces + autoscaler logs (due EOD)
- jorge: run the replay test in staging + reproduce (due +3h)
- sam: confirm billing ledger processing fix / backlog root cause (liaise with infra) (due +6h)
- oncall-rotations: consider short-term change to admission_controller config: increase default burst_credits or smooth depletion rate for Dedicated pools (proposal by tomorrow)
zephyr-bot: [note] incident created: INC-2024-582 (priority P2).
sam: Also we should add a playbook step: if ledger backlog detected, auto-increase burst_credits and signal scaling overrides to avoid mass 429s.
anya: I'll draft a quick runbook and post in #eng-sre after we confirm logs. For now marking as resolved-but-investigating since customer service restored. :white_check_mark:
jorge: Repro logs and replay results will determine if this needs an infra hotfix or just config tuning.
lena: Uploading artifacts to the incident ticket now.
nimbus-support: Thanks team — customer appreciated the quick mitigation. They asked for an ops summary and timeline which we'll attach to INC-2024-582.
sam: Great work. Leaving notes for retrospective on admission algorithm edge cases and ledger coupling.
anya: Closing thread for now, will reopen if replay shows race condition. :eyes:
